verdict: Accept as a structural repair with limited empirical confidence. curriculum_v2 resolves every review_v1 blocker and introduces no new blocking defect in coverage, boundaries, progression, mutual confidence, or generation. This is not an evaluation-backed success: the manifest contains zero C23-applicable held-out probes, so retrieval and transfer remain unverified.
mutual_confidence_findings: The planning leaves remain mutually coherent under cross-family counterexamples: c23.planning.audience transfers from analyzing novice operators to expert integrators because both require role, prior-knowledge, constraint, goal, and information-need analysis; c23.planning.evidence transfers from conflicting release notes to mixed benchmark claims because both require claim classification and gap control; c23.planning.structure transfers from first-use navigation to maintainer navigation because both require task-aligned page boundaries, hierarchy, progressive disclosure, and cross-references.

The reference leaves pass composite tests: c23.reference.operations compares an HTTP endpoint with a CLI command or emitted event; c23.reference.data-models compares a flat configuration object with a nested event contract; c23.reference.product-specifications compares hardware characteristics with software compatibility limits. Their domains and surfaces differ, but the respective central operations—caller-oriented operation description, contract-semantic documentation, and normalization of verified product facts—remain stable. c23.reference.product-specifications also retains a concrete boundary from c23.design.requirements: existing verified characteristics versus desired future behavior.

The instructional leaves pass supplied-context tests: c23.guides.how-to compares a command-line export with a firmware update; c23.guides.tutorials compares a novice application build with an operator setup exercise; c23.guides.explanations compares a causal mechanism explanation with a measured backpressure-strategy comparison; c23.guides.troubleshooting compares stale-cache diagnosis with authentication-failure diagnosis. The v2 probes supply workflows, behavior, measurements, logs, causes, or tested remedies, so success depends on the claimed documentation operation rather than unrelated technical discovery.

The design leaves pass within the claimed design-document regime: c23.design.requirements compares a latency need with an interface or security constraint; c23.design.proposals compares a data-ingestion architecture with a storage-migration choice; c23.design.decisions compares a library choice with a deployment-topology choice. Each pair preserves its central operation—verifiable requirement formulation, option evaluation, or recording a settled decision—even though technical subject matter changes.

The quality leaves pass their counterexample tests: c23.quality.constraints compares applying Markdown front matter and link conventions with applying a supplied XML-like documentation serialization; c23.quality.revision compares revising an API reference with revising an operator guide; c23.quality.maintenance compares an option rename with an endpoint deprecation. Transfer is credible when the publishing form and technical evidence are supplied. c23.quality.constraints should not be broadened to require undisclosed DITA, DocBook, or other format-specific expertise, but its current probes avoid that defect.
continuity_findings: c23.planning.audience→c23.planning.structure passes: both probes perform the full reader analysis, the representative uses its goals, knowledge, constraints, and information needs to determine architecture, and the entry adds one new operation—constructing a task-aligned heading sequence.

The four parent edges c23.planning→c23.reference, c23.planning→c23.guides, c23.planning→c23.design, and c23.planning→c23.quality pass. Each dependent probe performs reader/task analysis, claim control, document-form selection, and structure planning for the same artifact before adding, respectively, a reference entry, a procedure, measurable design framing, or publishing-compliant rendering. Unlike an unrelated deliverable concatenation, each plan governs the added document.

The reference-leaf edges pass: c23.planning.audience→c23.reference.operations and c23.planning.evidence→c23.reference.operations are exercised through caller analysis and a controlled interface-claim inventory before the entry adds operation-reference rendering; c23.planning.evidence→c23.reference.data-models adds field-contract documentation after claim control; c23.planning.evidence→c23.reference.product-specifications adds normalized specification rendering after claim control. The previously unnecessary c23.planning.structure edges are absent.

The instructional edges pass: c23.planning.audience→c23.guides.how-to adds safe procedural drafting for the analyzed operator; c23.guides.how-to→c23.guides.tutorials and c23.planning.audience→c23.guides.tutorials add learning scaffolding to a complete audience-appropriate procedure; c23.planning.audience→c23.guides.explanations and c23.planning.evidence→c23.guides.explanations add supported causal and tradeoff explanation; c23.guides.how-to→c23.guides.troubleshooting and c23.planning.evidence→c23.guides.troubleshooting add diagnostic routing over complete, evidence-backed corrective procedures.

The design edges pass: c23.planning.audience→c23.design.requirements and c23.planning.evidence→c23.design.requirements add atomic, measurable requirement formulation after stakeholder and claim analysis; c23.design.requirements→c23.design.proposals adds evaluation and recommendation between supplied viable approaches; c23.design.proposals→c23.design.decisions adds settled status, preserved rationale, consequences, and reconsideration conditions. The previously unnecessary c23.planning.structure→c23.design.proposals edge is absent.

The quality edges pass: c23.planning.audience→c23.quality.revision and c23.planning.evidence→c23.quality.revision add reader-centered revision after full audience and claim analysis; c23.quality.revision→c23.quality.maintenance adds propagation of a supplied change through compatibility, navigation, cross-references, and change records after the affected prose has been fully revised. c23.quality.constraints now has no artificial information-architecture prerequisite.

All seven review_v1 continuity blockers are repaired: c23.planning→c23.reference.operations was replaced by the narrower audience and evidence edges; c23.planning.structure→c23.reference.data-models, c23.planning.structure→c23.reference.product-specifications, c23.planning→c23.guides.how-to, c23.planning.structure→c23.design.proposals, and c23.planning.structure→c23.quality.constraints were removed; c23.planning.evidence→c23.reference.structured-records disappeared with the out-of-scope section.
other_findings: The prior containment blocker is repaired. c23.reference.structured-records was removed, while c23 and c23.reference now expressly exclude generic schema-instance generation. Discovery tasks c23-d01, c23-d05, c23-d09, c23-d13, and c23-d16 therefore have an explicit exclusion rationale based on their decisive JSON Schema validation operation.

The prior arbitrary-constraint blocker is repaired. c23.quality.constraints now requires technically complete documentation and documentation-specific templates or publishing forms, and excludes implementation work and artificial lexical games. Thus c23-d02 and c23-d06 remain outside C23 because their decisive operations are FFmpeg/Bash implementation and DOM/bookmarklet implementation, not documentation transformation.

The prior explanation blocker is repaired. c23.guides.explanations now supplies behavior descriptions, compatibility results, measurements, and reader briefs, and excludes conclusions that must be technically discovered. Consequently c23-d04 and c23-d15 do not anchor the leaf; their decisive work is unsupplied JavaScript expertise. c23-d08 and c23-d12 are likewise excluded as debugging or implementation tasks rather than documentation tasks.

Discovery accounting is complete: c23-d03, c23-d07, c23-d11, and c23-d14 are legal reasoning outside C23; c23-d01, c23-d05, c23-d09, c23-d13, and c23-d16 are generic schema-instance generation; c23-d02 and c23-d06 are programming tasks with incidental wrappers; c23-d04, c23-d08, c23-d12, and c23-d15 require technical discovery or implementation. c23-d10 maps primarily to c23.reference.product-specifications, but its closed-book iPhone recall and artificial per-word bracketing confound it, so it is weak rather than clean positive support.

Guidepost coverage is complete at the structural level: C23.1 maps to c23.reference and its three leaves; C23.2 maps to c23.guides.how-to and c23.guides.tutorials; C23.3 maps to c23.design and its requirements, proposals, and decision-record leaves. Discovery evidence remains sparse for most of these capabilities.

Evaluation evidence is insufficient. All 15 manifest entries apply only to C01, C07, C25, or C27; none applies to C23. The 15 corresponding annotations therefore provide no permissible held-out coverage, boundary, retrieval, or transfer evidence for any C23 section.

All six internal representatives perform coherent cross-child synthesis: c23 uses one weather-station release; c23.planning produces one documentation plan; c23.reference integrates one operation, its event model, and the associated device limits; c23.guides coordinates overview, tutorial, how-to, and troubleshooting around one deployment workflow; c23.design carries one service from needs through requirements, proposal, and decision; c23.quality revises, formats, and maintains one versioned operator guide after one rename. None merely concatenates unrelated child deliverables.
